page: Vultr vx1-m-2c-16g-120s is a memory-leaning virtual instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It provides two dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical AMD EPYC core running at a nominal 2.0 GHz base frequency, supported by 32 MB of Level 3 cache. The compute profile features an instruction set that includes AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16), AVX-VNNI, SHA-NI, and AES cryptography acceleration. The node is paired with 16 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU, alongside a bundled 120 GB NVMe SSD for local block storage and a single complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated hardware GPUs are provisioned on this instance.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded compute and compression throughput against cloud averages, registering 3013.38 on stress-ng single-core execution, 32.61 GB/s in gzip compression, and 14.3 GB/s in bzip3 single-threaded decompression. Geekbench single-core performance reached a score of 1778.0. However, aggregate multi-threaded execution reflects the hardware limit of two virtual threads, placing stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core (score 2278.0) in the lower quartile of multi-core test distributions. Memory throughput for large uncached 256 MB blocks yielded 26.94 GB/s read and 24.91 GB/s write bandwidth.

Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the configuration is cost-effective for tasks requiring generous memory headroom without necessitating parallel compute scaling. It exhibits lower absolute throughput on heavily parallel workloads, database operations (887.38 operations on PassMark), and larger language model inference. The instance is suited for caching tiers, memory-centric microservices, light data pipelines, background queuing workers, and staging environments where high memory density per core is prioritized over raw multi-threaded compute capacity.
description: Vultr vx1-m-2c-16g-120s is a memory-oriented virtual machine from the VX1 Cloud Compute line, featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs on a single physical AMD EPYC core running at 2.0 GHz with 32 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 16 GB of RAM, resulting in an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, complemented by 120 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and zero discrete GPUs. Hardware execution benefits from AVX-512, AES, and SHA-NI extensions. Performance benchmarks show capable single-threaded results, such as 32.61 GB/s gzip compression and strong stress-ng single-core compute, while aggregate multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth reflect its small two-thread allocation. The server delivers efficient resource provisioning for applications needing elevated RAM relative to processing power, making it appropriate for in-memory caching, single-threaded processing queues, lightweight backend APIs, and microservices requiring moderate capacity without paying for unneeded CPU threads.
